titleEn: When Sheep Say Baa, Stretch, Stretch!

pages.text: Outside the round window, sheep called baa, baa. They waited in a line at the pen gate. Pipo pulled the covers over his head. "A little more... It is warm as lamb's wool in here."
Mom, who ran the farm, peeped into his room. "Pipo, you said you would open the pen today. The sheep are waiting." "I will... after a little more sleep." He shook his head and slept again.
Much later, Pipo woke with a start. Outside, the pen gate was wide open. Sheep already grazed across the hill. "I wanted to open it..." He pouted.

Grandpa Sheep stood at the bedroom door with his walking stick. "In the old days, when sheep said baa, everyone did this." Keeping his stick planted, he stretched one hand high. Mom held Pipo's hand and stretched with him.

Hands stretch, toes stretch—his whole body grew long. Heavy eyelids lifted, and his body felt light. "Stretching opens my eyes! When sheep say baa, stretch, stretch!" His eyes became bright and awake.
"After stretching, open the round window. The sheep are waiting," Mom said softly. Pipo hopped off the bed and pushed the window with both hands. Creak—it opened.

Cool morning air drifted in. The sheep turned on the hill, saying baa. Pipo spread both hands and called, "Hello, sheep! When sheep say baa, stretch, stretch!" Now he felt he could reach the hill in one run.

Last, wash his face! Pipo cupped cold water from the tub by the well and splashed his face. He rubbed away sleep from his eyes, leaving his face bright and clean. Crouching by the tub, hands at his chest, he said, "I started the morning myself!"
The next morning, as soon as sheep said baa, Pipo held the pen handle. "One, baa means stretch, stretch! Two, window open and hello! Three, wash at the tub!" He had already done all three.

Pipo opened the gate wide, and sheep filed onto the hill. He ran to Mom and hugged her waist with both hands. "Mom, I opened it today!" Stretching chased sleep away. "When sheep say baa, stretch, stretch!"
